title: Russia recognizes the independence of Abkhazia and South Ossetia
body:
On 26 August 2008 Russian President Dmitry Medvedev signed a decree recognising South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent states. The decree followed a security council meeting in Sochi, and Russian forces remained in Georgia after the five-day war. South Ossetia had about 70,000 inhabitants and had held referendums in 1992 and 2006 that won no international recognition. Abkhazia, with about 250,000 inhabitants, had proclaimed independence unilaterally in July 1992.

Medvedev blamed Georgian President Mikheil Saakashvili for the attack to seize South Ossetia by force on 7 August and said that Saakashvili had "chosen genocide to fulfil his political plans". Residents of Sukhumi and Tskhinvali celebrated with gunfire and champagne.

Georgian officials condemned the step. Deputy Foreign Minister Giga Bokeria called it an annexation of Georgian territory, and National Security Council Secretary Alexander Lomaia said the decision had no legal force. The French foreign ministry called the move regrettable and reaffirmed its attachment to Georgia's territorial integrity, and US Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice also called it regrettable. Russia's RTS stock index fell nearly six per cent. Russian General Anatoly Nogovitsyn questioned increased NATO naval activity in the Black Sea and aid deliveries to Georgia's port of Poti.
